ai.description: *Bungarus lividus* reaches 1 meter. It is glossy black or dark brown with white crossbands. It lacks a vertebral ridge and possesses a rounded snout, distinguishing it from other krait species.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Bungarus lividus* is best distinguished by its uniform, glossy dark-brown to black dorsal coloration, which completely lacks the white crossbands found in other Indian kraits.
ai.habitat: *Bungarus lividus* inhabits moist deciduous forests and agricultural landscapes in the Himalayan foothills, typically ranging from lowlands up to 1,500 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Lesser Black Krait is strictly nocturnal, spending its daylight hours hiding in burrows or under debris before emerging at night to hunt for other snakes.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Bungarus lividus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–10 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing between August and October.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Lesser Black Krait (*Bungarus lividus*) is found in the Himalayan foothills of Northeast India, specifically in West Bengal, Assam, and Meghalaya.
